Abstract interface provided by Scintilla to lexers for reading and annotating the document. Offers text access, styling, folding levels, line states, indicator decoration, character classes, and code page information. Implemented by Scintilla core; lexers receive a pointer and must not delete it.

Abstract lexer interface version 5 used by Scintilla. Implementations perform lexical analysis and folding over a document via Lex and Fold, manage properties and word lists, and support substyles and style metadata. Lifetime is managed externally; Release() must be called by the owner when done.

Two anonymous enumerations defining integral constants dvRelease4 and lvRelease5 used as version identifiers for document and lexer interfaces. These are not types but introduce named constants; treated here as integer constants. Note: As anonymous enums, there is no distinct enum type name; the underlying type is int.

Abstract interface used to incrementally load data into a Scintilla document, typically from a background thread. Provides methods to append data, finalize and convert the loader into a document, and release the loader. Exact ownership semantics and status codes are defined by the Scintilla API; Release returns an integer status, AddData returns an SC_STATUS_* code, and ConvertToDocument yields an opaque document pointer.

Abstract interface for manipulating a document without a view, featuring version discovery for extended methods and reference-counted lifetime control (AddRef/Release). Intended to be implemented by Scintilla document objects; exposes no direct editing methods here.

Header-local constexpr integer constant with value 0, apparently related to document-editable release semantics. Not a type; included here only as an alias note if treated via typedef rules. No construction functions and no ownership relations. If strict type extraction is required, this should be ignored as it is not a type definition.

functions.name: sci::min
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
constexpr T sci::min(T x, T y) noexcept
functions.description: Returns the smaller of two values. Intended as a lightweight, constexpr alternative to std::min in the Scintilla namespace. Usage: pass two values of the same type T; the function compares x < y and returns x if true, otherwise returns y (ties return y). Suitable for compile‑time evaluation and in noexcept contexts.
requirements: Arguments x and y must have the same type T.
Type T must support a less-than comparison via operator< with a strict weak ordering.
T must be copyable or returnable by value.
No exceptions are thrown by this function (noexcept).

constexpr T sci::clamp(T x, T lower, T upper) noexcept
functions.description: Constrains a value x to the closed interval [lower, upper]. Returns lower if x < lower, upper if x > upper, otherwise returns x. import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target: Generate valid raw byte buffers that are useful for:
# - Scintilla::ILoader::AddData (arbitrary bytes, bounded <=1024 per call)
# - Scintilla::IDocument::SetStyles expects styles array of length span; FUZZ_PARAM_STR provides bytes
# We will craft bytes that are interesting for styling (patterns, ranges, repetitions) and
# also generic binary to feed the loader. Keep total <= 4096 bytes.

# Strategy:
# - Create a composition of several chunks:
#   * ASCII text with diverse characters and line endings (CR, LF, CRLF)
#   * Repeating style-byte patterns (0..255 ramps, stripes, primes)
#   * Random-length zero and 0xFF runs (to exercise padding and extremes)
#   * UTF-8 multibyte sequences and mixed widths (though loader treats raw bytes, documents may be UTF-8)
# - Randomize order and sizes, but keep each chunk valid as raw bytes.
# - Cap final size <= 2048 to stay safe; fuzzer caps per-use to 1024.


def _r(rand: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return rand.randint(a, b)


def _rand_ascii_text(rand: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix of letters, digits, punctuation, whitespace, tabs, varied EOLs
    choices = (
        [ord(c) for c in "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789"]
        + [ord(c) for c in " !@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{};:'\",.<>/?|`~"]
        + [9, 11, 12, 32]  # tab, vt, ff, space
    )
    out = bytearray()
    i = 0
    while i < length:
        t = _r(rand, 0, 9)
        if t == 0 and i + 2 <= length:
            # CRLF
            out += b"\r\n"
            i += 2
        elif t == 1 and i + 1 <= length:
            out.append(10)  # LF
            i += 1
        elif t == 2 and i + 1 <= length:
            out.append(13)  # CR
            i += 1
        else:
            out.append(rand.choice(choices))
            i += 1
    return bytes(out)


def _ramp(start: int, step: int, count: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(((start + i * step) & 0xFF for i in range(count)))


def _stripe(values: List[int], count: int) -> bytes:
    arr = bytearray()
    for i in range(count):
        arr.append(values[i % len(values)] & 0xFF)
    return bytes(arr)


def _utf8_sequences(rand: random.Random, count: int) -> bytes:
    # Generate valid UTF-8 sequences of varying lengths (1-4 bytes)
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(count):
        t = _r(rand, 1, 4)
        if t == 1:
            out.append(_r(rand, 0x20, 0x7E))  # printable ASCII
        elif t == 2:
            cp = _r(rand, 0x80, 0x7FF)
            out += chr(cp).encode('utf-8')
        elif t == 3:
            cp = _r(rand, 0x800, 0xFFFF)
            # avoid surrogates
            if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
                cp = 0xE000 + (cp - 0xD800)
            out += chr(cp).encode('utf-8')
        else:
            cp = _r(rand, 0x10000, 0x10FFFF)
            out += chr(cp).encode('utf-8')
    return bytes(out)


def _repeat_byte(b: int, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([b & 0xFF]) * max(0, n)


def _interesting_chunks(rand: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Chunk 1: ASCII text with mixed EOLs
    chunks.append(_rand_ascii_text(rand, _r(rand, 64, 256)))

    # Chunk 2: ramp 0..255
    chunks.append(_ramp(0, 1, _r(rand, 64, 512)))

    # Chunk 3: stripes of common style markers (0, 1, 2, 3, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xFF)
    chunks.append(_stripe([0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xFF], _r(rand, 64, 512)))

    # Chunk 4: zero run and FF run
    chunks.append(_repeat_byte(0x00, _r(rand, 16, 128)))
    chunks.append(_repeat_byte(0xFF, _r(rand, 16, 128)))

    # Chunk 5: UTF-8 sequences
    chunks.append(_utf8_sequences(rand, _r(rand, 16, 128)))

    # Chunk 6: small random blob
    chunks.append(rand.randbytes(_r(rand, 32, 128)))

    # Chunk 7: alternating prime-ish values to create patterns
    base = rand.choice([17, 31, 61, 97, 131, 197])
    step = rand.choice([3, 5, 7, 11])
    count = _r(rand, 64, 512)
    chunks.append(_ramp(base, step, count))

    return chunks


def _shuffle_and_trim(rand: random.Random, chunks: List[bytes], max_total: int) -> bytes:
    rand.shuffle(chunks)
    out = bytearray()
    for ch in chunks:
        remain = max_total - len(out)
        if remain <= 0:
            break
        if len(ch) <= remain:
            out += ch
        else:
            # take a slice; sometimes from start, sometimes middle, sometimes end
            mode = _r(rand, 0, 2)
            if mode == 0:
                out += ch[:remain]
            elif mode == 1:
                start = _r(rand, 0, len(ch) - remain)
                out += ch[start:start+remain]
            else:
                out += ch[-remain:]
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rand = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide a total size between 256 and 2048 bytes (fuzzer will take up to 1024)
    total = _r(rand, 256, 2048)
    chunks = _interesting_chunks(rand)

    # Occasionally prepend a small header-like section with common text to help SetText scenarios
    header = bytearray()
    if rand.random() < 0.6:
        header += b"// Scintilla fuzz seed:" + str(seed).encode('ascii') + b"\r\n"
        header += b"int main() { return 0; }\n"
        header += b"#define MACRO 1\n/* comment */\n"
    body = _shuffle_and_trim(rand, chunks, max_total=max(0, total - len(header)))
    data = bytes(header) + body

    # Ensure not exceeding 4096 bytes
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 24) -> str:
    # Typical identifier: start with letter or underscore, then letters/digits/underscore
    start_chars = string.ascii_letters + "_"
    body_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-."  # include dash and dot to exercise lexer variety
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)

def _pack_cstring(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode as UTF-8 null-terminated c-string
    b = s.encode('utf-8', 'strict')

    b = b.replace(b"\x00", b"_")

    out = b"".join(_pack_cstring(t) for t in toks)

    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4095] + b"\x00"

    return out

        parts.append(line)
        parts.append(mix_eol(rng))

    # Include known-language-like snippets to exercise StyleAt/word classifications
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        parts.append(rng.choice(LANG_SNIPPETS))
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(mix_eol(rng))

    # Insert blocks of lorem words with varied wrapping and punctuation
    words = LOREM_WORDS.copy()
    rng.shuffle(words)
    cur = []
    line_len = rng.randint(40, 120)
    curlen = 0
    for w in words[: rng.randint(15, len(words))]:
        token = w
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            token += rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            token += rng.choice([",", ";", ":", ".", "!"])
        if curlen + 1 + len(token) > line_len:
            parts.append(" ".join(cur))
            parts.append(mix_eol(rng))
            cur = []
            curlen = 0
            line_len = rng.randint(30, 100)
        cur.append(token)
        curlen += len(token) + 1
    if cur:
        parts.append(" ".join(cur))
        parts.append(mix_eol(rng))

    # Empty lines and whitespace-only lines
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        parts.append("")
        parts.append(mix_eol(rng))
        parts.append(rnd_indent(rng))
        parts.append(mix_eol(rng))

    # Deliberately long line (near 200 chars) to exercise LineEnd scanning
    long_line = rnd_line(rng, rng.randint(150, 220))
    parts.append(long_line)
    parts.append(mix_eol(rng))

    # Trailing segment without newline to exercise end-of-buffer handling
    tail = rnd_line(rng, rng.randint(10, 80))
    parts.append(tail)

    # Combine and trim to max_bytes and also ensure not empty
    doc = "".join(parts)
    if not doc:
        doc = "\n"
    if len(doc.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")) > max_bytes:
        # Trim by characters but ensure not cut inside CRLF badly: we just cut by bytes safely
        enc = doc.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")[:max_bytes]
        doc = enc.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        if not doc:
            doc = "\n"
    return doc


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Produce 1 to 3 candidate documents and pick one with varied features
    count = rng.randint(1, 3)
    candidates = [build_document(rng, max_bytes=1000) for _ in range(count)]

    # Prefer candidate with the highest line count under 512 to exercise arrays
    def score(doc: str) -> int:
        # Count lines by splitting on \n and \r patterns: approximate using any of \n/\r
        nl = sum(1 for ch in doc if ch in "\n\r") + 1
        unique_eols = sum(1 for e in EOLS if e in doc)
        uni = sum(1 for u in UNICODE_SAMPLES if u in doc)
        return min(nl, 512) * 3 + unique_eols * 5 + uni

    chosen = max(candidates, key=score)
    return chosen.encode("utf-8")
